batches.title: An Opinionated Guide to ML Research
batches.note: The PPO/RLHF creator's framework for choosing problems: concept- vs execution-driven, why novelty-seeking fails, how to build taste by close-reading seminal papers.

batches.title: LLM Architecture Gallery
batches.note: The visual one: a side-by-side picture-book of how each major LLM is wired (attention, norm placement, MoE, positional encoding). The fastest way to see what actually changed model-to-model.

batches.title: Machines of Loving Grace
batches.note: Anthropic's CEO on what 'AI going well' concretely looks like — compressed timelines on disease, biology, poverty. Research taste applied at civilizational scale: which problems are worth a decade.

batches.title: Practicing AI Research
batches.note: The CoT author decomposes research into four learnable skills — idea selection, experiment design, writing, and the underrated one: distributing your results. The execution layer under Schulman's concept/execution split.

batches.title: Principles of Effective Research
batches.note: The fourth meta-essay to sit beside Hamming, Schulman and Steinhardt. Problem-creators beat problem-solvers, difficulty is a poor proxy for importance, and your real edge is a stack of complementary skills no rival bothered to combine. The Kolmogorov move (bury a hard problem inside a larger structure so the work pays even if the core never cracks) is worth the read alone.

batches.title: The Bitter Lesson
batches.note: Calibrate every research bet against the one claim that keeps being right: scale plus search beats hand-crafted structure, always.

batches.title: The Shift from Models to Compound AI Systems
batches.meta: Matei Zaharia, Jonathan Frankle, Naveen Rao et al. (Databricks) · essay
batches.note: The field-defining manifesto: SOTA now comes from compound systems (model + retrieval + tools + verifiers), not monolithic models. The paradigm every agent builder — including you — is living inside.

batches.title: Understanding Reasoning LLMs
batches.note: The cleanest synthesis of the four ways to build reasoning models — inference-time scaling, SFT, RLVR/GRPO, search — and why DeepSeek-R1-Zero's verifiable-reward move worked. Backs your 'verifiable reward goes vertical' principle with the person who explains it best.

batches.title: You and Your Research
batches.note: Extract the specific habits (working on important problems, keeping your door open to make luck, selling your work) that separate Nobel output from competent mediocrity.

batches.title: Your AI Product Needs Evals
batches.note: From 30+ production builds: the #1 cause of failed AI products is no eval system. The operator's version of 'build the verifier first' — with the Rechat case study as the concrete loop.

batches.title: nanochat: the best ChatGPT that $100 can buy
batches.note: One hackable codebase that trains a talkable ChatGPT clone end to end for about $100: BPE tokenizer, pretraining on FineWeb, mid-training, SFT, RL with GRPO, an eval harness and KV-cache inference behind a chat UI. The post-training half the GPT-2 build skips, in one readable pipeline you can own start to finish.

batches.title: A Recipe for Training Neural Networks
batches.note: The craft under "stay close to the run": nets fail silently, so go simple to complex, form one hypothesis per step, and never trust a result you can't explain.

batches.title: Agents
batches.note: What actually determines agent capability: the tool set and the planning architecture, taxonomized with crisp tradeoffs. The mental model for why your LangGraph topology choices are non-cosmetic.

batches.title: Ahead of AI (magazine.sebastianraschka.com)
batches.note: The site itself: his running deep-dives on how each new LLM and training method actually works. Follow it; the architecture comparison and reasoning-LLM essays above live here, and he updates them as the frontier moves.

batches.title: Deep Learning Curriculum
batches.note: A frontier researcher's personal reading-and-build path: Transformers internals, scaling laws, training at scale, RL, optimization, interpretability, each chapter pairing the core papers with an implementation exercise. Study what the frontier studies, in its order, from someone who built WebGPT and RL scaling-laws work.

batches.title: How I Think About My Research Process: Explore, Understand, Distill
batches.note: DeepMind's mech-interp lead on his actual loop for open-ended research, and the junior mistake of forcing hypothesis-tests while you're still exploring. The heuristic that decides which threads to chase: optimize for information gained per unit time, and treat curiosity-driven surface-area as real work.

batches.title: How To Become A Mechanistic Interpretability Researcher
batches.note: Nanda's path to the frontier, from someone who trained ~50 juniors into the field: learn the minimal basics fast, then learn by doing through throwaway 1-5 day mini-projects, then 1-2 week sprints with deliberate continue-or-pivot calls. The how-to-skill-up-on-your-own companion to his Explore/Understand/Distill loop above.

batches.title: How to win a best paper award (doing research that matters)
batches.note: A decade retrospective from Google Brain/DeepMind, now Anthropic: the single most important skill is taste in which problems are worth solving, then how he generates and filters ideas, executes, writes, and ships for impact over citation count. Pure problem-selection, first-person, new for 2026.

batches.title: Interpretability Dreams
batches.note: A masterclass in choosing the tractable sub-problem that opens a whole agenda instead of charging the big question head-on.

batches.title: LLM Powered Autonomous Agents
batches.note: The canonical architectural map of agent systems — planning (CoT/ToT/ReAct/Reflexion), memory, tool use, failure modes. The reference cited by almost every serious agent paper. Read for the taxonomy before you build.

batches.title: Research Taste Exercises
batches.note: Turns "taste" into trainable drills, like "if another group published your paper, would you be excited to read it?" The closest thing to a how-to for the skill labs actually hire for.

batches.title: Research as a Stochastic Decision Process
batches.note: The algorithm for running a project once you've chosen it: de-risk the load-bearing assumption first and order experiments by information gained per unit of time.

batches.title: Spinning Up as a Deep RL Researcher
batches.note: An OpenAI researcher's deliberate-practice curriculum for deep RL: what math and DL to front-load, re-implementing REINFORCE through PPO and DDPG in their simplest form, and the experiment hygiene (fair baselines, multi-seed, ablations, precommitted final runs) that separates trustworthy results from noise.

batches.title: The Big LLM Architecture Comparison
batches.note: Side-by-side teardown of 11+ frontier architectures (DeepSeek, Llama 4, Gemma 3, Qwen3, Grok). The practitioner's lens for reading an architecture paper and knowing which choices are cosmetic vs load-bearing.

batches.title: The Scaling Hypothesis
batches.note: The method, not the conclusion: how to read scaling papers and extrapolate further than the authors dare, holding a contrarian thesis with the right uncertainty.

batches.title: The Second Half
batches.note: The builder of ReAct, SWE-bench and tau-bench argues the working RL recipe (strong priors plus reasoning-as-action) now beats incremental method work, so the frontier value moves from solving problems to defining and evaluating them. The payload: today's benchmarks hide unstated i.i.d. and auto-execution assumptions, and that gap is where the next real research lives. Build the eval, not the next method.

batches.title: The Ultra-Scale Playbook
batches.note: 4,100+ distributed-training experiments distilled into one empirical reference for training LLMs across hundreds of GPUs — data/tensor/pipeline parallelism, memory, throughput. The real 'how training works at scale,' not theory.

batches.title: The engineering challenges of scaling interpretability
batches.note: The team behind Scaling Monosemanticity on the infrastructure that made it possible: a multi-pass distributed shuffle and a sharded activation-caching pipeline to visualize millions of SAE features. The load-bearing lesson is that engineering, not ideas, is the bottleneck to interpretability progress.

batches.title: Two Alignment Threat Models
batches.note: A clean taxonomy — under-elicited (sloppy) vs scheming (deceptive) models — that reframes alignment work. 1,500 words from the person now running Anthropic's alignment science.

batches.title: Aggregation Theory
batches.note: The structural reason internet products win by owning demand, not supply — the mechanic behind every aggregator. Essential before designing any platform or marketplace.

batches.title: Building Effective Agents
batches.meta: Erik Schluntz & Barry Zhang (Anthropic) · essay · ~20 min
batches.note: Ground truth for which architectural shape (prompt chaining, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer) fits which problem — use it to audit whether your LangGraph topology is solving the right class of problem.

batches.title: Crossing the Uncanny Valley of Conversational Voice
batches.meta: Sesame (Schalkwyk, Kumar, Lyth et al.) · article · ~15 min
batches.note: Speech treated as a contextual problem, not text-to-audio: a single-stage model on residual-vector-quantized tokens, the transformer split at the zeroth codebook so a big backbone handles semantics and a small decoder reconstructs acoustics, and training the decoder on a random 1/16 of frames to kill the memory bottleneck.

batches.title: Generative AI's Act Two
batches.meta: Sonya Huang & Pat Grady (Sequoia) · essay · ~15 min
batches.note: The retention test that exposes wrappers: apply the 60-85% DAU/MAU benchmark to Skale before you trust any growth number.

batches.title: Optimizing AI Inference at Character.AI
batches.note: Character.AI trains natively in int8 to kill the train/serve mismatch, stacks multi-query plus hybrid local/global attention plus cross-layer KV-sharing for a 20x-plus KV-cache reduction, and runs a stateful prefix cache hitting 95% to cut serving cost 33x. The literal proof that the moat is the serving system, not the weights.

batches.title: A Beginner's Guide to Category Design
batches.note: Category design as a discipline equal to product and company design — why the category king captures most of the economics, and how to design a category rather than compete for demand.

batches.title: AI Integration and Modularization
batches.note: Christensen's integration/modularization lens applied to AI — use it to decide where in the stack to plant your flag so you sit in the integrated position, not the squeezed modular one.

batches.title: Good news: AI Will Eat Application Software
batches.meta: Alex Immerman & Santiago Rodriguez (a16z) · essay · ~12 min
batches.note: The counterpositioning play: why per-outcome pricing structurally beats seat-based incumbents who can't cannibalize their own revenue.

batches.title: Reflections on Three Years of Building LangChain
batches.note: The honest tension between ease-of-use and production reliability in agent frameworks — read it as the maker of the thing you build Skale on, so you know what LangGraph fixed and what's still unsolved.

batches.title: Replit AI Manifesto
batches.meta: Michele Catasta & Amjad Masad · essay · ~10 min
batches.note: The vertical-integration-as-moat argument plus a concrete agentic feedback loop (Reflect-Evaluate-Percolate-Learn) you can steal the shape of.

batches.title: We're Solving Graphics Backwards
batches.note: Runway's CEO names the field's primitive problem: classical graphics solved control first then rendering, generative AI inverted it, so the move is to invent control primitives native to the latent space instead of retrofitting triangles. A short, contrarian-and-right reframe of what a generative-media moat is.

batches.title: Agent Design Is Still Hard
batches.note: Reporting from inside a real agent build by the creator of Flask: skip the high-level SDKs because model differences force your own abstraction, prefer explicit cache control, reinforce the objective on every tool return rather than once up front, and isolate failures in throwaway sub-agents that report only outcomes.

batches.title: Software 2.0
batches.note: The 2017 mental model (weights ARE the program) that explains why "refactoring" and "code review" mean something different when you direct machines.

batches.title: The Engineering Executive's Primer
batches.note: The clearest map of what a CTO actually owns vs. delegates, drawn from Stripe/Uber/Calm/Carta — read it as the org-design layer under your agent fleet.

batches.title: The Rise of the AI Engineer
batches.note: The supply-demand argument that named a job category: millions of software engineers versus thousands of ML researchers means API-first AI engineering eats the training loop, roughly 1000x cheaper per iteration. The payload is a staffing-and-leverage call about where to put eng headcount, not a how-to.

batches.title: Crafting Engineering Strategy
batches.note: Writing strategy that actually changes what gets built next quarter — the rarest CTO skill, with Wardley maps and systems models.

batches.title: If you are good at code review, you will be good at using AI agents
batches.note: The counterweight to harness-as-moat, from a staff engineer at GitHub: line-level nitpicking is near-useless with agents, and the durable skill is structural judgment, catching when the agent is committing to an architectural dead end and reasoning about the code that could have been written.

batches.title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Tasks
batches.meta: METR (Kwa, West, Becker et al.) · paper
batches.note: The primary source for the task-horizon curve you're betting on: the methodology and doubling-time confidence intervals behind "build for 18 months out."

batches.title: My LLM Coding Workflow Going into 2026
batches.note: Ground-level discipline for directing agents without losing control: spec-first, small chunks, always review.

batches.title: Ralph Wiggum as a 'software engineer'
batches.note: A genuinely contrarian harness primitive: a single deterministic bash loop running one focused task on a fresh context each pass makes failure modes observable and tunable, and can beat elaborate multi-agent orchestration running on a stale context. The originating account, from someone who built a compiler this way.

batches.title: The Engineer/Manager Pendulum
batches.note: Why deliberately swinging back to IC keeps you technically sharp enough to direct the machines well.
